question: Four robots at a crossing each hold one cell and each wants the next robot's cell in a loop. What happens?
options: The last robot in the loop yields by itself
Deadlock, so none of them can ever move
They take turns and pass one at a time
explanation: Each robot in the loop waits for the next one to move and none can, so the wait never ends. That is deadlock.

question: You draw your crossing as a wait-for graph. What does an arrow from robot A to robot B mean?
options: A and B are both heading to the same goal
A needs the cell that B is standing on
A will reach its goal before B does
explanation: An arrow from A to B means A is waiting for the cell B stands on, so the graph shows who blocks whom.

question: Your crossing has frozen and you inspect the wait-for graph. What in it proves a deadlock?
options: A closed loop of waiting arrows
A node with two arrows leaving it
A long, unbroken chain of arrows
explanation: Every robot on a closed loop waits for the next one, so none of them can move first.

question: You make your robots claim their whole route before entering. Which deadlock condition does that remove?
explanation: A robot enters only when its whole route is free, so no robot ever waits while holding cells. That removes hold-and-wait.

question: You add more robots and the reservation throughput levels off instead of rising. Why?
options: Each robot drives slower when the floor is crowded
Reservation itself deadlocks once the fleet is large
Whole routes block each other, so few run at once
explanation: Claimed routes block other robots, so adding robots does not let more of them run at once. That is the price of preventing deadlock.

question: Two robots at your crossing face each other in one lane. What does the wait-for graph show?
options: A single arrow from one robot to the other one
A cycle of length 2, with an arrow each way
A chain of three robots ending at a free cell
explanation: Facing each other, each robot needs the cell the other stands on, so A waits for B and B waits for A, which is a loop of two.
